defect.locator_note: lake/Adams v. Williams__80ad69.json treatment.derivation lane1_negative and lane2_top_cited; content_page.md Treatment & subsequent history
defect.problem: The unqualified good-law/no-negative-treatment presentation cannot be verified from the disclosed record. The lake repeats a good_law field, but its treatment derivation also reports audit-needed lanes and 223 proposed negative treatment edges, including overruled, abrogated, criticized, questioned, and superseded_by_statute labels. Under the default-to-refuted rule, the current treatment assertion is too certain until those proposed edges are audited or cleared.
defect.proposed_fix: Do not state 'No negative treatment' or an unqualified 'does not disturb Adams' treatment note until the R15 treatment audit is complete. Tighten to: 'Current lake field labels Adams good_law, but proposed negative-treatment candidates require audit; no final disclosed treatment override is recorded.'

reasons: The page says 'No negative treatment,' but the lake treatment derivation has audit_needed true for lane1_negative and lane2_top_cited.

The disclosed lake has 223 proposed treatment edges: 98 overruled, 10 abrogated, 16 criticized, 93 questioned, and 6 superseded_by_statute; all are proposed and all have field_iii mentioned, so they do not prove Adams is bad law, but they prevent verifying the stronger no-negative-treatment claim from disclosed evidence alone.
The weight label Binding - SCOTUS is supported by the lake identity fields; the defect is the currency/treatment certainty, not the court-weight label.
residual_risks: A completed treatment audit may ultimately confirm good_law, but that confirmation is not disclosed in the present files.
Full review of the proposed negative edges would require the underlying citing-case treatment evidence.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Separate the lake's current good_law field from the unresolved treatment-audit status, and remove the categorical 'No negative treatment' sentence unless the proposed negative edges are cleared.
